correctness.rationale: Reconstructed all domain restrictions and incidence fibers. W has pure dimension D=M+n(d-1), generic irreducible fibers, and is irreducible. Rank M is exhibited by M distinct coordinate Segre points in a coordinate hyperplane. The rank-drop inverse image is proper; its fibers are projective spaces of dimension >=1, hence rank-drop image codim>=2. The conormal parameter count is M-1 and the tangency incidence dimension <=D-d, yielding R1 on rank M. The published CM theorem provides S2; Serre proves normality. Tangency is asserted only as a necessary condition for singularity, not sufficient.

value.rationale: Uniform normality and absence of divisorial nonnormality across arbitrarily many factors/dimensions and configurations is a structural invariant not supplied by existing prime/CM calculations. Its rank-drop and conormal codimension bounds explain why hyperplane reconstruction is unique in codimension one and constrain singular strata, relevant to the three-flatland-camera image model. This is not a textbook normalization restatement or an arbitrary slice; it resolves a natural global geometric property of the newly studied maximal-minor schemes.
